q: What is the role of reduced NAD in linking the Krebs cycle to the electron transport chain?
options: It carries high-energy electrons from the matrix to complex I, then returns as NAD+
It transports ATP from the matrix into the intermembrane space for export to the cytoplasm
It carries O2 from the cytoplasm to complex IV, where the oxygen is reduced to water
It carries the CO2 released in the Krebs cycle out through both of the mitochondrial membranes
explanation: Most of the energy from glucose oxidation is captured in reduced NAD (10 per glucose) and reduced FAD (2). NADH diffuses to complex I on the matrix side of the inner membrane, donates 2 electrons (releasing H+) and becomes NAD+ again, ready to accept more hydrogen in the link reaction and Krebs cycle.
